title: Cabled rectangular stole
subtitle: An aran-weight stole with a central rope cable flanked by seed stitch borders.
excerpt: A rectangular stole in aran-weight wool with a central 12-stitch rope cable running the full length, flanked by 3-stitch seed stitch borders on each side. Finished size approximately 38 cm wide by 165 cm long, blocked. About 500 g of aran yarn.
sourceNotes: The rope cable (C6F/C6B alternating) is a standard technique documented in Barbara Walker, A Treasury of Knitting Patterns (1968), §Cable Patterns, as the basic 6-stitch rope cable. Seed stitch borders for rectangular wraps appear widely in 20th-century knitting manuals. Construction here is original.

knitting.gaugeText: 18 sts × 24 rows = 10 × 10 cm in seed stitch on 5 mm needles.
knitting.gaugeInPatternStitch: 12 sts × 16 rows = 6 × 8 cm in rope cable on 5 mm needles.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Approximately 38 cm wide by 165 cm long.

glossaryTerms.definition: A cable that crosses in the same direction on every cable row, creating a twisted rope appearance. A C6F rope cable crosses to the left; a C6B rope cable crosses to the right.
An alternating knit-purl pattern worked so that knit stitches sit over purls and purls sit over knits on every row. The result is a dense, flat fabric with a pebbly texture on both sides.

content.text: A rectangular stole in aran-weight wool with a 12-stitch
rope cable
running the full length of the centre, flanked by
seed stitch
borders. Finished size approximately 38 × 165 cm.

The stole is worked lengthwise: the cast-on runs the full 165 cm length and the stole grows across 38 cm as rows are added. The central cable crosses every 6 rows. Budget about 500 g (about 1,000 m / 1,090 yards) of aran wool.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: About 500 g (1,000 m / 1,090 yards) of aran-weight yarn

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 5 mm (UK 6 / US 8) circular needle, 120 cm or longer

content.text: Gauge

18 stitches and 24 rows to 10 cm over seed stitch on 5 mm needles. The cable panel draws in approximately 20%: the 12-stitch panel knits to about 5.5 cm rather than the 6.7 cm it would measure in plain knit. This is accounted for in the cast-on count. If your seed stitch gauge reads 16 stitches per 10 cm, add 8 stitches to the cast-on to compensate.
Stitches used

items.name: C6F
items.qty: cable 6 front: slip 3 sts to cable needle, hold front, k3, k3 from cable needle

content.text: Pattern
Cast on

Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 297 stitches (3 seed border + 12 seed + 12 cable + 12 seed + 3 seed = 42 stitches per 10 cm of width; adjusted to 297 for 165 cm length at 18 sts / 10 cm). For the long-tail allow approximately 175 cm of tail.
Row structure
All rows: seed 3, seed 18 (to cable marker), SM, k12 (or C6F on cable rows), SM, seed 18, seed 3.
Cable row (every 6th row): replace k12 with C6F.
Seed stitch: *k1, p1; repeat from *. On the next row knit the purls and purl the knits.
Continue until width (number of rows) reaches 38 cm (approximately 91 rows at 24 rows / 10 cm).
Bind off
Standard bind-off in pattern (seed over seed sections, k over cable section). Bind off loosely to match the cast-on edge.
Stitch count check-ins
Every 10 rows: stitch count must remain 297. The cable never changes stitch count. If the count shifts, a seed stitch k2tog or yo occurred in error.
Common faults

Seed stitch reverting to rib: the knit-over-knit / purl-over-purl pattern was followed instead of knit-over-purl. Seed stitch requires that every stitch be worked opposite to the stitch below it. On set-up, the cast-on creates a knit bump on the needle; the first row over these must alternate k and p starting with a p over the cast-on knit.
Cable crossing every 4 rows instead of 6: the cable row tracker was miscounted. Mark every 6th row on the needle with a slip-on marker at the cable crossing to track the interval.
Blocking

Steam-block lightly, as aran cables benefit from steam rather than wet-blocking. Hold a steam iron 3 cm above the fabric and allow the steam to penetrate without pressing. Do not press down on the cable; the cable texture is the design.
Care
Hand wash in cool water, lay flat to dry. The seed stitch borders dry faster than the cable centre; check the cable is fully dry before folding.
What to try next

Replace the single central rope cable with three parallel 6-stitch rope cables, each separated by 4-stitch seed stitch columns. This creates a fully cabled surface in a wider stole using approximately the same yardage.
